subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Which host-owned configuration mutations, if any, may installed plugins synchronously veto?
rationale: The answer determines recovery availability, secret exposure, compatibility guarantees, and whether the API can honestly promise that relevant writes cannot bypass validation.

options.title: Gateway RPC Policy
options.body: Expose a trusted typed veto for config.set, config.patch, and config.apply while excluding doctor, recovery, setup, and host-owned security writes.

options.title: Global Write Policy
options.body: Invoke plugins from the shared configuration mutation layer and accept that plugin failures can block every host configuration and recovery path.

options.title: No Mandatory Veto
options.body: Keep built-in validation authoritative and retain optional before_tool_call policies or explicit plugin-owned mutation APIs without a new interceptor.

recommendation.title: Gateway RPC Policy
recommendation.body: Expose a trusted typed veto for config.set, config.patch, and config.apply while excluding doctor, recovery, setup, and host-owned security writes.

likelyOwner.reason: The live discussion shows the clearest product-routing engagement and an explicit keep-open assessment of the remaining public API gap.
